_comment: Checks and numbers for the Part 1 grader. part1/quiz.py repeats the same numbers for the notebook's own checks, so change both together. The lab image ships this file, so it never holds an answer: the multiple-choice key lives only in the assessment image (grader/answer_keys/).

part1.title: Part 1 Assessment
part1.label: Part 1
part1.pass_rule_text: You pass when T1, T2, T4 and the T5 search pass and at least 6 of the 8 multiple-choice answers are correct. T3, T6, T7 and whether your T5 window shows a labelled collision are reported to you but do not decide the result.

checks.text: T1: VIOS lists the sensor id in t1.vios_sensor_id, under the name in t1.vios_name (rain_check or rain_check_<n>), and it has a recorded timeline.
T2: t2.frames equals the number of RT-CV frame records Elasticsearch holds for sensorId rain_check (mdx-raw-2025-01-01), and t2.top_type is the most frequent object type in those records.
T3: t3 comes from a decoded mdx-raw message of this clip. t3.sensor_id is rain_check, and Elasticsearch holds a rain_check frame with id t3.frame_id at t3.timestamp.

T4: At chunk_duration 10, RT-VLM split the 30 s clip into 3 or 4 chunks. At chunk_duration 0 it made 1 chunk. With 8 sampled frames, every full chunk reported frame_count 8 (a short last chunk may report fewer). The caption index default_<t4.file_id, with - replaced by _> holds your captions.

T5: a search of the four search clips for t5.query returns your window first. It is the same file, and its start and end are within 0.1 s of the top hit's. Times are seconds from 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z, the anchor the embedding index uses.
T5 (reported): your window overlaps a labelled collision in that clip.
T6: t6.answer_object_id is the object that a nested kNN on objects.embedding.vector ranks first for the query object t6.query_object_id, in a frame other than the query's own.

T7: t7.requests_per_day is 8,640, one 10-second chunk every 10 seconds for a day. t7.busy_seconds_per_day is within 15 percent of 8,640 x t7.latency_ms / 1000: the seconds RT-VLM would spend on one camera per day if it answered one request at a time.
Multiple choice: at least 6 of the 8 answers in answers.json are correct.
